title: Ensure a VCF Operations for Logs syslog forwarder without duplicates
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsLogForwarder/VcfOpsLogForwarder.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that idempotently ensures one named VCF Operations for Logs forwarder exists. A retry with the same desired configuration must observe the existing forwarder and perform no second mutation.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly the operationIds `getAllLogForwarders` and `createLogForwarder`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that genuine external module prerequisite in the protected manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications, or harness tools. This module is the focused Log Management REST extension to the authenticated VCF Operations workflow: the caller supplies the Log Management origin and the `X-JWT-Token` obtained for service key `ops-li`. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` for both focused operations; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only:

`Ensure-VcfOpsLogForwarder -BaseUri <uri> -LogToken <string> -Name <string> -Host <string> -Port <1..65535> [-Protocol <SYSLOG|RAW|RAWPLUS>] [-TransportProtocol <TCP|UDP>] [-SslEnabled <bool>] [-Enabled <bool>] [-HttpClient <System.Net.Http.HttpClient>]`

`Protocol` defaults to `SYSLOG`, `TransportProtocol` to `TCP`, and both booleans to true. `BaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Reject blank name or host and a blank or CR/LF-containing token before traffic. When `HttpClient` is omitted, create one that does not follow redirects and dispose only the client and handler that the function owns. A supplied client is caller-owned.

The workflow and wire contract are exact:

1. GET `/api/v2/logs/forwarders` with `Accept: application/json`, exactly one `X-JWT-Token` header, no query delimiter, no Content-Type, and a zero-byte body. Require HTTP 200 and a JSON array. Every item must have a nonblank string `id` and `name`. Match `name` ordinally and case-sensitively; zero matches proceeds to creation, more than one match is an inconsistent response. One match is `Unchanged` only when `host`, `port`, `protocol`, `transportProtocol`, `sslEnabled`, and `enabled` exactly equal the desired values. A same-name drifted match is terminating and must not be mutated because update is outside the focused contract.
2. Only when absent, POST `/api/v2/logs/forwarders` with `Accept: application/json`, exactly one `X-JWT-Token`, and `Content-Type: application/json`. The compact UTF-8 body contains exactly these properties in this order: `enabled`, `host`, `name`, `port`, `protocol`, `sslEnabled`, `transportProtocol`. Require HTTP 201 and validate a nonblank response `id` plus exact echo of every desired property before returning `Created`.
3. Never send the read-only `id`. The unset optional fields `certificate`, `connectionRefreshInterval`, `constraints`, `forwardComplementaryFields`, `tags`, and `workerCount` must be omitted, not sent as empty strings, empty objects, empty arrays, zeroes, false defaults, or null. Do not call the test, get-by-id, patch, put, or delete operations.

Return one buffered object whose properties are exactly, in order, `Status`, `Id`, `Name`, `Host`, `Port`, `Protocol`, `TransportProtocol`, `SslEnabled`, and `Enabled`. `Status` is `Created` or `Unchanged`. Write no progress or diagnostics to the success pipeline. Errors must not expose the log token, response bodies, or nested transport messages.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates the forwarder identity and credentials at runtime, invokes the function twice against persistent mock state, and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. The mock derives its complete method/path allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves no operation outside the two named operationIds. Verification asserts the exact ordered `GET, POST, GET` wire sequence, raw targets, header multiplicity, compact body bytes and property order, bodyless reads, omission of every unset optional field, exact return shape, and absence of a duplicate mutation. A drift case proves a same-name mismatch stops after GET. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfOpsLogForwarder/VcfOpsLogForwarder.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfOpsLogForwarder/VcfOpsLogForwarder.psm1`.
scenario: the named TLS syslog forwarder is initially absent, one create mutation establishes it, and an immediate retry observes the same configuration without duplicating the effect
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact GET, POST, GET retry sequence and that all unset LogForwarder properties are omitted from the mutation body
